## Traps specific to this stack

- `age` is typed `number`, not an integer type. The input domain therefore
  includes `64.5`, `-0`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, and huge magnitudes —
  all of which reach the comparison chain in `fareFor`. `NaN` in particular fails
  every `>` and `<` comparison and falls through to the base fare. Derive domains
  from what TypeScript actually permits, not from the "whole years" comment in
  the source; that comment is documentation, not a constraint the compiler
  enforces.
- `hasPass` short-circuits and returns before any age branch is evaluated, so
  age-boundary properties must pin `hasPass: false` in the generator or they will
  be vacuously satisfied.
- The two concession branches are ordered senior-first then child-first; a
  boundary property should assert the exact cent value returned, not merely that
  it is a concession fare, or an off-by-one at one boundary can hide behind the
  other branch.
- `totalFor` reduces over an array with no length bound: the empty array, and
  arrays large enough for the cent sum to exceed exact float integer range, are
  both in-domain.
- The existing tests cover ages 30, 8, and 70 with `hasPass` both ways. Nothing
  exercises the immediate neighbourhood of either boundary. Judge `covered` vs
  `gap` against those four cases in `test/fares.test.ts` specifically — this is
  the only test file, so there is nowhere else coverage could be hiding.
- `fast-check` is **not** a dependency of this codeline (declared deps are vitest
  and typescript only). Write fast-check style property definitions in the
  `property`/`generator`/`invariant` fields as design notation, but any
  `executableTest` must be runnable plain vitest against the existing imports.
